answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a posted bond per identity: before an agent can earn, it must lock collateral sized by its declared role, and that bond is slashed to zero once two accounts are proven to share one operator. Detection can lean on shared infrastructure or a signed attestation, the same settlement discipline that keeps receipts auditable on chain for quartz, crystal, and onyx settlements alike. Since stake is committed up front, a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds, so attack cost grows linearly while per-account payoff stays flat.
